Docs: sync the crate table in CLAUDE.md to all 91 workspace members

---

CLAUDE.md's own "Keeping This File Up to Date" section makes the crate table the single source of truth for the workspace. A table that omits shipped connectors misleads every future contributor (and Claude session) about what exists. Pure docs, fully verifiable, zero code risk.

- `CLAUDE.md` — add the missing rows to the crate table (mirroring the existing one-line-description style), covering at minimum: `faucet-source-azure-blob`, `faucet-sink-azure-blob`, `faucet-source-pubsub`, `faucet-sink-pubsub`, `faucet-common-pubsub`, `faucet-source-clickhouse`, `faucet-sink-clickhouse`, `faucet-common-clickhouse`, `faucet-source-redshift`, `faucet-sink-redshift`, `faucet-common-redshift`. ===== ISSUE #437 =====
Refactor+test: extract a pure `progress_ratio` in backfill metrics
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs::set_progress` (~L43) computes a completion ratio inline (`if planned == 0 { 1.0 } else { done / planned }`) and immediately feeds it to a `metrics` gauge macro, so the divide-by-zero guard and clamping can't be unit-tested. Extract the arithmetic into a tiny pure fn and test it.

## Motivation
The `0/0`, `done < planned`, and `done == planned` cases are exactly where a progress bar goes wrong (NaN, >1.0). A pure `progress_ratio(done, planned) -> f64` makes them testable without touching the metrics recorder.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs` — pull the ratio logic into `fn progress_ratio(done: usize, planned: usize) -> f64`, call it from `set_progress`, and add a `#[cfg(test)]` module covering: `planned == 0` → `1.0`; `done == 0, planned > 0` → `0.0`; `done == planned` → `1.0`; `done < planned` → the expected fraction; (optionally) `done > planned` clamped to `1.0`.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `progress_ratio` exists as a pure fn and is used by `set_progress`.
- Tests cover the four/five cases above and never produce NaN.
- `cargo test -p faucet-cli` passes.

## Out of scope
- Changing what metric is emitted or its name.


===== ISSUE #436 =====
Tests: cover `RunStreamOptions` builder methods
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`crates/core/src/observability/options.rs` defines the `RunStreamOptions` builder (`with_name`, `with_row`, `with_run_id`, `with_state`, `with_dlq`, `with_cancel`, `with_adaptive`, `with_quality`, …) but has no `#[cfg(test)]` module and isn't exercised by `crates/core/tests/*`.

## Motivation
These builders are pure and directly shape pipeline behavior (bookmarks, DLQ, delivery, cancellation). A small test that each `with_*` sets exactly its field and that chaining composes protects a widely-used public API with almost no effort — an ideal first contribution.

## Proposed change
- `crates/core/src/observability/options.rs` — add a `#[cfg(test)]` module asserting that each `with_*` populates the corresponding `Option`/field, leaves the others at default, and that a chained builder composes all set fields.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/core/src/observability/options.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- Each builder method has at least one assertion.
- A chaining test sets several fields and verifies all are retained.
- `cargo test -p faucet-core` passes.

## Out of scope
- Testing the streaming loop that consumes the options.


===== ISSUE #435 =====
Tests: broaden `glob_match` edge-case coverage (SFTP source)
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs` has a hand-rolled backtracking `glob_match` (~L93) used to filter remote listings. Its test module (~L188) covers `*` / `?` / literals / multi-star, but not the off-by-one boundary cases a backtracking matcher classically gets wrong.

## Motivation
Glob matching decides which remote files a run ingests; a subtle boundary bug means silently skipping or over-including files. The missing cases are exactly the ones worth pinning.

## Proposed change
- `crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs` — add cases to the existing `#[cfg(test)]` module, e.g.:
  - `glob_match("", "")` → `true`
  - `glob_match("", "x")` → `false`
  - `glob_match("a?", "a")` → `false` (trailing `?` with exhausted input)
  - `glob_match("abc", "ab")` → `false` (pattern longer than name, no star)
  - `glob_match("*", "")` → `true`
  - `glob_match("a*", "a")` → `true`

Fix `glob_match` only if one of these reveals an actual bug; otherwise this is a pure test-hardening change.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- The new assertions are added and pass (or a real bug is fixed to make them pass).
- `cargo test -p faucet-source-sftp` passes.

## Out of scope
- Replacing the matcher with a glob crate.

CLI: `faucet schema --list` to enumerate valid schema targets
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---

`faucet schema <target>` supports many targets (`config`, `source`, `sink`, `transform`, `dlq`, `replication`, `backfill`, `execution`, `resilience`, `sla`, …) but there is no way to discover the valid set from the CLI. ## Motivation
Discoverability: users shouldn't have to read the source or the docs to learn which schema targets exist. This mirrors the self-describing spirit of `faucet list`.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/cli.rs` — add `#[arg(long)] pub list: bool` to `SchemaArgs` (~L1011); make the positional target optional when `--list` is passed.
- `cli/src/commands/schema.rs` — when `list` is set, print the target names (the `SchemaTarget` variants dispatched at ~L11-40) and return before dispatching.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/cli.rs`, `cli/src/commands/schema.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `faucet schema --list` prints every valid target name and exits 0.
- Existing `faucet schema <target>` behavior is unchanged.
- A test asserts the listing includes known targets (e.g. `source`, `sink`, `dlq`).
- `docs/book/src/reference/cli.md` mentions `--list`.

Kafka sink: make Schema Registry encode errors actionable
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---

When a Confluent Schema-Registry value format is selected on the Kafka sink but no Schema Registry client was built, encoding fails with a terse message that states the problem but not the fix.

## Motivation
`FaucetError::Config("ConfluentAvro selected but no SchemaRegistryClient")` (and the Protobuf / JsonSchema twins) tell the user *what* is wrong but not *how* to fix it. A one-line hint naming the missing config field turns a head-scratcher into a self-service fix.

- `crates/sink/kafka/src/encode.rs` — extend the three error strings at ~L47 (Avro), ~L58 (Protobuf), ~L69 (JsonSchema) to point at the fix, e.g.:
  `"value format 'confluent_avro' requires a Schema Registry client — set `schema_registry.url` (and any auth) in the Kafka sink config"`.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/kafka/src/encode.rs` (three sites).

## Acceptance criteria
- All three messages name the missing config (`schema_registry.url`) and the selected format.
- A unit test asserts the improved message text for at least one format.
- No behavior change beyond the message.

## Out of scope

===== ISSUE #430 =====
Validation: S3 / GCS sink configs accept an empty `bucket`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
The object-store sink configs require a `bucket` name but never reject an empty string. An empty `bucket` should be a load-time config error, not a runtime API failure.

## Motivation
Fail-fast validation: a blank `bucket` (typo, unset `${env:...}`) currently sails through config load and only blows up when the first upload hits the cloud API with an opaque error. A typed `FaucetError::Config` at load time is far clearer.

## Proposed change
- `crates/sink/s3/src/config.rs` — `bucket` at ~L28. Add `pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), faucet_core::FaucetError>` that returns `FaucetError::Config` when `bucket` is empty (also call `validate_batch_size` if the config carries one), and invoke it at construction.
- `crates/sink/gcs/src/config.rs` — `bucket` at ~L29. Same treatment.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/s3/src/config.rs`, `crates/sink/gcs/src/config.rs` (+ construction sites).

## Acceptance criteria
- Building either sink with an empty `bucket` returns a typed `FaucetError::Config` naming the field.
- Valid configs are unaffected.
- Unit tests cover empty-`bucket` rejection and a valid config passing.

## Out of scope
- Source-side validation (tracked in the source-config `validate()` issue).

CLI: add `--json` output to `faucet validate`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`faucet validate` is a CI-oriented command but only emits prose (`ok: '...' rows=...`, per-row role lines). Add a `--json` flag that prints a structured validation summary so CI systems can assert on it programmatically.

## Motivation
Teams gate merges on `faucet validate`. Parsing prose is brittle; a stable JSON summary (config name, row count, per-row source/sink/roles, run/skip selection decision) makes the command reliable in automation and consistent with the `--json` flags already on `list`/`search`/`conformance`.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/cli.rs` — add `#[arg(long)] pub json: bool` to `ValidateArgs` (~L978).
- `cli/src/commands/validate.rs` — the human path (`run`, ~L17; `println!` lines ~L56-64 and ~L147-206) already computes per-row data. Collect it into a `#[derive(Serialize)]` summary struct and emit it with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` when `--json` is set.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/cli.rs`, `cli/src/commands/validate.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `faucet validate <cfg> --json` prints a JSON object with at least: config `name`, `row_count`, and a `rows` array (each with `id`, `source`, `sink`, role/parent info, and the RUN/skip decision when a selector is active).
- Non-`--json` output is unchanged.

CLI: add `--json` output to `faucet list`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`faucet list` only prints human-readable columns via `println!`. Sibling commands already expose a machine-readable `--json` flag (`faucet search`, `faucet conformance`), so this is a small consistency/ergonomics gap. Add `--json` so the compiled-in sources/sinks/transforms/state-stores (and the `--available` registry rows) can be consumed by tooling and CI.

## Motivation
Users scripting around faucet (dashboards, CI checks, editor integrations) currently have to scrape the printed table. A JSON mode makes `list` composable and consistent with the rest of the CLI surface.

- `cli/src/commands/list.rs` — in `run` (~L17) and `list_available` (~L44), when `json` is set, serialize the collected data to a JSON object (arrays of `{name, description, tier}` for sources/sinks, names for transforms/state-stores) with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` instead of the printed columns.

- `cli/src/cli.rs`, `cli/src/commands/list.rs`

===== ISSUE #415 =====
Examples: add a runnable example config for an uncovered connector pair
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary

Add one or more runnable, inline-commented `cli/examples/<src>_to_<sink>.yaml` configs for a common connector pair that lacks an example today — e.g. `kafka_to_clickhouse.yaml`, `mongodb_to_parquet.yaml`, or `postgres_cdc_to_kafka.yaml` — and wire it into `examples/README.md`.

## Motivation

Copy-paste-and-it-runs examples are the single biggest lever on first-run success, and every connector pair with a real example is one more entry point for a newcomer (and one more indexable page). Writing a grounded example is the lowest-risk possible first PR — pure config, no Rust — and it forces the author to actually exercise the connectors, which surfaces doc gaps.

## Proposed design

- Pick a pair not already covered under `cli/examples/` (check the directory first to avoid duplicates).
- Write the YAML **inline-commented** in the house style: annotate each section (source, auth, pagination/replication, transforms, sink, state, and `matrix:` if used). Reuse field names verified against the connector's `config.rs` / `faucet schema` — do not invent fields.
- Add a row to `examples/README.md` mapping the example to the infra it needs (no-infra / local-stack via `examples/docker-compose.yml` / cloud-creds) and the exact run command.
- If the pair needs local infra not already in `examples/docker-compose.yml`, either pick a pair whose infra already exists, or note the addition.
- `faucet validate <the-new-file>` must pass in CI-style (no run required).

## Edge cases & failure modes

- Secrets must use `${env:...}` / `${secret:...}` interpolation — never hardcode credentials.
- Keep it runnable: prefer pairs whose infra is already in the compose stack so `docker compose up` + `faucet run` works end-to-end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `cli/examples/<pair>.yaml`, inline-commented, field names verified against the connectors.
- [ ] `faucet validate` passes on it.
- [ ] `examples/README.md` mapping entry added (infra + run command).
- [ ] No duplication of an existing example.

## Out of scope

- New connectors or infra images (this is config + docs only).

## References

- Pattern to copy: the existing `cli/examples/*.yaml` and the `examples/README.md` mapping.
- Docs-sync rules in `CLAUDE.md` ("Keeping Docs & Artifacts in Sync"); grounded-in-real-configs rule.
- Contributor on-ramp from **#91** / **#314**; roadmap epic **#38**.


===== ISSUE #61 =====
Connectors: friendly connector_name() overrides + opt-in internal spans
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
Roll out friendly `connector_name()` overrides and (where they add value) per-connector internal spans across the remaining 29 built-in connectors. The decorator layer that landed with #31 already covers the universal metric set automatically using the stripped `type_name` default — e.g. a `PostgresSource` gets `connector=\"PostgresSource\"` without code changes. This issue is the polish: replace the default with a short snake-case label and optionally add connector-internal spans under the reserved `faucet.<connector>.<operation>` namespace.

## Motivation
- **Friendlier metric labels.** `connector=\"rest\"` reads better than `connector=\"RestStream\"` in dashboards and alerts, and matches CLI YAML `type: rest`.
- **Connector-internal observability** (e.g. per-HTTP-request count, retry events, Kafka partition rebalance events) is currently absent. The reserved namespace is defined; each connector decides what's worth emitting.
- The decorator approach (#31) means this work is now genuinely incremental — every connector lands independently.

## Connectors that still need overrides
Sources: graphql, xml, grpc, postgres, postgres-cdc, mysql, sqlite, s3, mongodb, redis, webhook, csv, elasticsearch, parquet, kafka.
Sinks: bigquery, postgres, snowflake, mysql, sqlite, s3, mongodb, redis, csv, elasticsearch, http, stdout, parquet, kafka.

(REST source and JSONL sink already landed in #31.)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every source/sink crate listed has `fn connector_name(&self) -> &'static str { \"<friendly>\" }` (one-liner, snake_case label matching the YAML `type:`).
- [ ] Per-connector internal spans where they add value (REST request, BigQuery insert_all, Kafka partition events, postgres-cdc commit, parquet row-group, etc.) — opt-in per crate using the `faucet.<connector>.<operation>` namespace.
- [ ] Each crate's README mentions the connector label.

## Suggested PR shape
One PR per connector or per small connector group. Each PR is one-line (or a handful of lines for internal spans) plus a unit test. Trivially mergeable; no shared coordination.

## Out of scope
- Cross-cutting changes to the decorator / Pipeline (already done in #31).
- New metric or span names outside the reserved namespace.

## References
- Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-23-observability-otel-prometheus-design.md`
- Roadmap epic: #38
- Parent: #31

# MongoDB collection → local Parquet files.
#
# Streams documents out of a MongoDB collection (with a filter, projection, and
# sort) and writes them as columnar Parquet — the Arrow schema is inferred from
# the first batch of records, so no schema declaration is needed. Ideal for
# snapshotting an operational collection into an analytics-friendly file format.
#
# Infra: MongoDB from `examples/docker-compose.yml` (the `mongodb` service).
# The Parquet sink writes to the local filesystem — no cloud credentials needed.
#
# Run:
#   docker compose -f examples/docker-compose.yml up -d mongodb
#   faucet validate cli/examples/mongodb_to_parquet.yaml
#   faucet run      cli/examples/mongodb_to_parquet.yaml
version: 1
name: mongodb_to_parquet

pipeline:
  source:
    type: mongodb
    config:
      # Standard MongoDB connection string. Point at your replica set / cluster.
      connection_uri: mongodb://localhost:27017
      database: shop
      collection: orders
      # Server-side filter — only completed orders are exported.
      filter:
        status: completed
      # Return just the fields we care about (1 = include). Drop `_id` so the
      # ObjectId doesn't need type handling downstream.
      projection:
        _id: 0
        customer_id: 1
        total: 1
        currency: 1
        created_at: 1
      # Deterministic ordering makes re-runs reproducible.
      sort:
        created_at: 1
      # Cap the export; remove for a full-collection dump.
      limit: 500000
      # Driver-side cursor batch size (network round-trip granularity).
      cursor_batch_size: 1000

  sink:
    type: parquet
    config:
      # Local filesystem destination. A path ending in `.parquet` writes a single
      # file; a directory path rolls over to `<uuid>.parquet` files instead.
      destination:
        type: local_path
        path: ./out/orders/
      # Codec applied to each column chunk: uncompressed | snappy | gzip | zstd | lz4.
      compression: zstd
      # Roll over to a new file every N rows (directory mode) to cap file size.
      max_rows_per_file: 200000
      # Rows per Arrow record batch handed to the writer. `0` = write whatever
      # the source hands over as one batch (recommended for Parquet, which
      # prefers fewer, larger row groups).
      batch_size: 0

Clears a batch of open **`good first issue`** items in one PR. Each is independent; grouped for a single review pass.

| Issue | Change |
|------|--------|
| #427 | `faucet list --json` — structured listing of sources/sinks/transforms/state stores (also `list --available --json`). |
| #428 | `faucet validate --json` — structured validation summary for CI (matrix **and** topology modes); prose report suppressed under `--json`. |
| #432 | `faucet schema --list` — enumerate the valid schema targets compiled into the binary. |
| #61  | Friendly snake-case `connector_name()` overrides for the **24 remaining** built-in connectors (matching the YAML `type:`), each with a specific-value test + a README observability note. |
| #430 | Fail-fast validation rejecting an empty `bucket` on the S3 / GCS sinks (typed `FaucetError::Config` at construction). |
| #431 | Actionable Kafka Schema-Registry encode errors — name the wire format and `schema_registry.url`. |
| #437 | Extract a pure, unit-tested `progress_ratio(done, planned)` in backfill metrics (0/0, over-count clamping). |
| #436 | Tests for the `RunStreamOptions` builder methods. |
| #435 | Boundary-case tests for the SFTP `glob_match` matcher (empty inputs, trailing `?`, over-long pattern). |
| #434 | Tests for `faucet init` `resolve_kinds` / `unknown_kind_err`. |
| #433 | Test for the `is_topology()` predicate. |
| #415 | Runnable `cli/examples/mongodb_to_parquet.yaml` (MongoDB → local Parquet) + `examples/README.md` mapping. |

## Notes

- **#61** deliberately changes `connector_name()` from the default stripped type name (e.g. `"CsvSource"`) to the friendly label (`"csv"`); the two registry tests that asserted the old default were updated accordingly. Two sinks (postgres, mysql) place their specific-value assertion in a testcontainer-gated conformance test (matching the pre-existing placement), so those two one-line methods are only exercised under Docker.
- **`--json` for `validate`** keeps the human report byte-identical when the flag is absent.
- Docs: `docs/book/src/reference/cli.md` documents all three new flags.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p faucet-core --lib` (RunStreamOptions builders), `-p faucet-cli --lib` (schema/list/init/topology/backfill/registry), `-p faucet-cli --test cli_end_to_end` (new `list --json` / `schema --list` / `validate --json` tests), `-p faucet-sink-kafka --features schema-registry` (encode messages), `-p faucet-sink-s3` / `-p faucet-sink-gcs` (bucket validation), `-p faucet-source-sftp` (glob).
- `cargo check --tests` across all 24 connector crates (conformance edits compile).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p faucet-core --all-features` clean.
